Examples of tooltip usage below: ```html ``` The tooltip text is surrounded in double quotes. The styles of the tooltip are set by the class `.mermaidTooltip`. ```mermaid-example flowchart LR A-->B B-->C C-->D click A callback "Tooltip for a callback" click B "https://www.github.com" "This is a tooltip for a link" click C call callback() "Tooltip for a callback" click D href "https://www.github.com" "This is a tooltip for a link" ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR A-->B B-->C C-->D click A callback "Tooltip for a callback" click B "https://www.github.com" "This is a tooltip for a link" click C call callback() "Tooltip for a callback" click D href "https://www.github.com" "This is a tooltip for a link" ``` > **Success** The tooltip functionality and the ability to link to urls are available from version 0.5.2. ?> Due to limitations with how Docsify handles JavaScript callback functions, an alternate working demo for the above code can be viewed at [this jsfiddle](https://jsfiddle.net/yk4h7qou/2/). Links are opened in the same browser tab/window by default. It is possible to change this by adding a link target to the click definition (`_self`, `_blank`, `_parent` and `_top` are supported): ```mermaid-example flowchart LR A-->B B-->C C-->D D-->E click A "https://www.github.com" _blank click B "https://www.github.com" "Open this in a new tab" _blank click C href "https://www.github.com" _blank click D href "https://www.github.com" "Open this in a new tab" _blank ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR A-->B B-->C C-->D D-->E click A "https://www.github.com" _blank click B "https://www.github.com" "Open this in a new tab" _blank click C href "https://www.github.com" _blank click D href "https://www.github.com" "Open this in a new tab" _blank ``` Beginner's tip—a full example using interactive links in a html context: ```html 
    flowchart LR
        A-->B
        B-->C
        C-->D
        click A callback "Tooltip"
        click B "https://www.github.com" "This is a link"
        click C call callback() "Tooltip"
        click D href "https://www.github.com" "This is a link"
``` ### Comments Comments can be entered within a flow diagram, which will be ignored by the parser. Comments need to be on their own line, and must be prefaced with `%%` (double percent signs). Any text after the start of the comment to the next newline will be treated as a comment, including any flow syntax ```mermaid-example flowchart LR %% this is a comment A -- text --> B{node} A -- text --> B -- text2 --> C ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR %% this is a comment A -- text --> B{node} A -- text --> B -- text2 --> C ``` ## Styling and classes ### Styling links It is possible to style links. For instance, you might want to style a link that is going backwards in the flow. As links have no ids in the same way as nodes, some other way of deciding what style the links should be attached to is required. Instead of ids, the order number of when the link was defined in the graph is used, or use default to apply to all links. In the example below the style defined in the linkStyle statement will belong to the fourth link in the graph: ``` linkStyle 3 stroke:#ff3,stroke-width:4px,color:red; ``` It is also possible to add style to multiple links in a single statement, by separating link numbers with commas: ``` linkStyle 1,2,7 color:blue; ``` ### Styling line curves It is possible to style the type of curve used for lines between items, if the default method does not meet your needs. Available curve styles include `basis`, `bumpX`, `bumpY`, `cardinal`, `catmullRom`, `linear`, `monotoneX`, `monotoneY`, `natural`, `step`, `stepAfter`, and `stepBefore`. For a full list of available curves, including an explanation of custom curves, refer to the [Shapes](https://d3js.org/d3-shape/curve) documentation in the [d3-shape](https://github.com/d3/d3-shape/) project. Line styling can be achieved in two ways: 1. Change the curve style of all the lines 2. Change the curve style of a particular line #### Diagram level curve style In this example, a left-to-right graph uses the `stepBefore` curve style: ``` --- config: flowchart: curve: stepBefore --- graph LR ``` #### Edge level curve style using Edge IDs (v11.10.0+) You can assign IDs to [edges](#attaching-an-id-to-edges). After assigning an ID you can modify the line style by modifying the edge's `curve` property using the following syntax: ```mermaid-example flowchart LR A e1@==> B A e2@--> C e1@{ curve: linear } e2@{ curve: natural } ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR A e1@==> B A e2@--> C e1@{ curve: linear } e2@{ curve: natural } ``` ```info Any edge curve style modified at the edge level overrides the diagram level style. ``` ```info If the same edge is modified multiple times the last modification will be rendered. ``` ### Styling a node It is possible to apply specific styles such as a thicker border or a different background color to a node. ```mermaid-example flowchart LR id1(Start)-->id2(Stop) style id1 fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:4px style id2 fill:#bbf,stroke:#f66,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff,stroke-dasharray: 5 5 ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR id1(Start)-->id2(Stop) style id1 fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:4px style id2 fill:#bbf,stroke:#f66,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff,stroke-dasharray: 5 5 ``` #### Classes More convenient than defining the style every time is to define a class of styles and attach this class to the nodes that should have a different look. A class definition looks like the example below: ``` classDef className fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:4px; ``` Also, it is possible to define style to multiple classes in one statement: ``` classDef firstClassName,secondClassName font-size:12pt; ``` Attachment of a class to a node is done as per below: ``` class nodeId1 className; ``` It is also possible to attach a class to a list of nodes in one statement: ``` class nodeId1,nodeId2 className; ``` A shorter form of adding a class is to attach the classname to the node using the `:::`operator as per below: ```mermaid-example flowchart LR A:::someclass --> B classDef someclass fill:#f96 ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR A:::someclass --> B classDef someclass fill:#f96 ``` This form can be used when declaring multiple links between nodes: ```mermaid-example flowchart LR A:::foo & B:::bar --> C:::foobar classDef foo stroke:#f00 classDef bar stroke:#0f0 classDef foobar stroke:#00f ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR A:::foo & B:::bar --> C:::foobar classDef foo stroke:#f00 classDef bar stroke:#0f0 classDef foobar stroke:#00f ``` ### CSS classes > **Note:** Applying styles to Mermaid nodes via external CSS (e.g., `.cssClass > rect { fill: ... }`) does **not** work reliably. Mermaid's internal styles are injected with `!important` and scoped to the SVG element ID, giving them higher specificity than external CSS rules. External CSS will be silently overridden. > > The recommended approach is to use the `classDef` syntax shown in the [Classes](#classes) section above, which works correctly and is the intended styling mechanism. > > If external CSS is strictly required, every property must use `!important` to override Mermaid's styles — but this is not recommended. **Working approach — use `classDef` instead:** ```mermaid-example flowchart LR A:::myStyle --> B classDef myStyle fill:#ff0000,stroke:#ffff00,stroke-width:4px ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR A:::myStyle --> B classDef myStyle fill:#ff0000,stroke:#ffff00,stroke-width:4px ``` ### Default class

### Turning an Animation On

Once you have assigned an ID to an edge, you can turn on animations for that edge by defining the edge’s properties:

```mermaid-example
flowchart LR
  A e1@==> B
  e1@{ animate: true }
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A e1@==> B
  e1@{ animate: true }
```

This tells Mermaid that the edge `e1` should be animated.

### Selecting Type of Animation

In the initial version, two animation speeds are supported: `fast` and `slow`. Selecting a specific animation type is a shorthand for enabling animation and setting the animation speed in one go.

**Examples:**

```mermaid-example
flowchart LR
  A e1@--> B
  e1@{ animation: fast }
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A e1@--> B
  e1@{ animation: fast }
```

This is equivalent to `{ animate: true, animation: fast }`.

### Using classDef Statements for Animations

You can also animate edges by assigning a class to them and then defining animation properties in a `classDef` statement. For example:

```mermaid-example
flowchart LR
  A e1@--> B
  classDef animate stroke-dasharray: 9,5,stroke-dashoffset: 900,animation: dash 25s linear infinite;
  class e1 animate
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A e1@--> B
  classDef animate stroke-dasharray: 9,5,stroke-dashoffset: 900,animation: dash 25s linear infinite;
  class e1 animate
```

In this snippet:

- `e1@-->` creates an edge with ID `e1`.
- `classDef animate` defines a class named `animate` with styling and animation properties.
- `class e1 animate` applies the `animate` class to the edge `e1`.

**Note on Escaping Commas:**
When setting the `stroke-dasharray` property, remember to escape commas as `\,` since commas are used as delimiters in Mermaid’s style definitions.

## New arrow types

There are new types of arrows supported:

- circle edge
- cross edge

### Circle edge example

```mermaid-example
flowchart LR
    A --o B
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A --o B
```

### Cross edge example

```mermaid-example
flowchart LR
    A --x B
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A --x B
```

## Multi directional arrows

There is the possibility to use multidirectional arrows.

```mermaid-example
flowchart LR
    A o--o B
    B <--> C
    C x--x D
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A o--o B
    B <--> C
    C x--x D
```

### Minimum length of a link

Each node in the flowchart is ultimately assigned to a rank in the rendered
graph, i.e. to a vertical or horizontal level (depending on the flowchart

```
subgraph title
    graph definition
end
```

An example below:

```mermaid-example
flowchart TB
    c1-->a2
### Default class

If a class is named default it will be assigned to all classes without specific class definitions.

```
    classDef default fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:4px;
```

## Basic support for fontawesome

It is possible to add icons from fontawesome.

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: docs
commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: chrome-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: built-in-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: anthropic-skills:deep-research
commands.description: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly. (claude.ai sync)

commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. content.content:
## Expanded Node Shapes in Mermaid Flowcharts (v11.3.0+)

Mermaid introduces 30 new shapes to enhance the flexibility and precision of flowchart creation. These new shapes provide more options to represent processes, decisions, events, data storage visually, and other elements within your flowcharts, improving clarity and semantic meaning.

New Syntax for Shape Definition

Mermaid now supports a general syntax for defining shape types to accommodate the growing number of shapes. This syntax allows you to assign specific shapes to nodes using a clear and flexible format:

```
A@{ shape: rect }
```

This syntax creates a node A as a rectangle. It renders in the same way as `A["A"]`, or `A`.

### Complete List of New Shapes

Below is a comprehensive list of the newly introduced shapes and their corresponding semantic meanings, short names, and aliases:

| **Semantic Name**                 | **Shape Name**            | **Short Name** | **Description**                             | **Alias Supported**                                              |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bang                              | Bang                      | `bang`         | Bang                                        | `bang`                                                           |
| Browser                           | Browser                   | `browser`      | Browser window                              |                                                                  |
| Bucket                            | Bucket                    | `bucket`       | Object storage bucket                       |                                                                  |

"""Run a stock, hermetic `git merge` of (base, o, t) and return (clean, merged_text)."""
import os
import subprocess
import tempfile


def merge(base: str, o: str, t: str, fname: str):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        home = os.path.join(d, "home")
        os.mkdir(home)
        repo = os.path.join(d, "repo")
        os.mkdir(repo)
        env = {
            "PATH": os.environ["PATH"],
            "HOME": home,
            "XDG_CONFIG_HOME": os.path.join(home, ".config"),
            "GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM": "1",
            "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL": "/dev/null",
            "GIT_AUTHOR_NAME": "f", "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL": "f@example.invalid",
            "GIT_COMMITTER_NAME": "f", "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL": "f@example.invalid",
            "LC_ALL": "C",
        }

        def git(*a, check=True):
            return subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=repo, env=env, check=check,
                                  capture_output=True, text=True)

        def put(text):
            with open(os.path.join(repo, fname), "w", newline="") as f:
                f.write(text)

        git("init", "-q", "-b", "main")
        put(base); git("add", fname); git("commit", "-q", "-m", "base")
        git("checkout", "-q", "-b", "t")
        put(t); git("commit", "-q", "-am", "t")
        git("checkout", "-q", "main")
        git("checkout", "-q", "-b", "o")
        put(o); git("commit", "-q", "-am", "o")
        r = git("merge", "--no-edit", "-q", "t", check=False)
        unmerged = git("ls-files", "-u", "--", fname).stdout.strip()
        with open(os.path.join(repo, fname), newline="") as f:
            merged = f.read()
        markers = any(l.startswith(("<<<<<<<", ">>>>>>>")) or l == "=======" for l in merged.split("\n"))
        clean = r.returncode == 0 and not unmerged and not markers
        return clean, merged

    texts = [f["base"], f["o"], f["t"], merged]
    note = ""

            fs = [model.fences(x) for x in texts]
            note = "fences=%s " % [len(x) for x in fs]
            dia = [x[0] if len(x) == 1 else None for x in fs]
        else:

        res = None
        if clean and all(dia):
            try:

            except model.ParseError as e:
                note += "MERGED-PARSE-ERROR %s " % e
        elif not all(dia[:3]):
            note += "INPUT-FENCE-PROBLEM "
    except model.ParseError as e:
        note += "PARSE-ERROR %s " % e
        res = None
    status = "clean" if clean else "CONFLICT"
    print("=" * 70)

    if res:
        print("  model:   ", res["records"], "exposed", res["exposed"])
        print("  newlints:", res["new_lints"])
    if verbose or "-m" in sys.argv:
        print(merged)

"(§3). Both fences parse, so the path is not E. Tier B (§5.4: every G0 record; L6 also fails). The "
   "fence count makes the merged state unjudgeable for any other category. Not exposed: the diagram's "
   "model is identical in all three inputs.")

FENCE = d("""
    ```mermaid
    graph TD
        user([Customer]) --> web[Storefront]
        web --> cart[Cart service]
        cart --> stock[(Inventory)]
        web --> search[Search]
    ```
    """)
TILDE = FENCE.replace("```mermaid", "~~~mermaid").replace("```\n", "~~~\n")
B = ("# Storefront\n\nThe storefront is the customer-facing web application.\n\n" + FENCE +
     "\n## Getting started\n\nRun `npm ci` and then `npm run dev`.\n\n"
     "## Design notes\n\nCart and inventory share a database today; see ADR 12.\n")
O = ed(B, (FENCE + "\n", ""), ("see ADR 12.\n", "see ADR 12.\n\n" + TILDE))
T = ed(B, (FENCE + "\n", ""), ("Run `npm ci` and then `npm run dev`.\n",
                                "Run `npm ci` and then `npm run dev`.\n\n## Components\n\n" + FENCE.rstrip("\n") + "\n"))
fx("v19-g0-both-move-tilde-md", "D", B, O, T, False, [("G0", ["<path>"], "B")],
   "Both legs move the diagram away from the introduction: O to the design notes, rewriting the fence "
   "with tildes; T to a new Components section. Identical deletions merge once, both insertions stay. "
   "G0 (§5.3): two Mermaid fences in the merged file (one backtick, one tilde, both match §3's opener), "
   "where each input has one. Both parse, so not E. Tier B (G0). Not exposed: the three input models "
   "are equal.")

FENCE = d("""
    ```mermaid
    flowchart TD
        push[git push] --> hook[Webhook]
        hook --> runner[CI runner]
        runner --> cache[(Build cache)]
        runner --> report[Status check]
    ```
    """)
B = ("# CI setup\n\nThis repository uses a self-hosted runner.\n\n" + FENCE +
     "\n## Secrets\n\nSecrets are injected from the vault at job start.\n\n"
     "## Appendix\n\nOld runner hostnames are listed in `hosts.txt`.\n")
O = ed(B, (FENCE + "\n", ""), ("listed in `hosts.txt`.\n", "listed in `hosts.txt`.\n\n" + FENCE))
T2 = FENCE.replace("    runner --> report[Status check]\n",
                   "    runner --> report[Status check]\n    runner --> artifacts[(Artifact store)]\n")
T = ed(B, (FENCE + "\n", ""), ("injected from the vault at job start.\n",
                                "injected from the vault at job start.\n\n## Pipeline\n\n" + T2.rstrip("\n") + "\n"))
fx("v20-g0-move-and-edit-md", "D", B, O, T, False, [("G0", ["<path>"], "B")],
   "O moves the diagram to the appendix unchanged. T moves it under a new Pipeline heading and adds an "
   "artifact store to it. Both remove the fence from the top identically; both insertions survive. "
   "G0 (§5.3): two Mermaid fences in the merged file, one in each input. Both parse, so not E. Tier B. "
   "Not exposed: T only adds a node and an edge.")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- G1
B = d("""
    flowchart LR
        ui --> gateway
        gateway --> sso
        gateway --> orders
        orders --> users
        orders --> stock
        sso --> users
    """)

     "## Design notes\\n\\nCart and inventory share a database today; see ADR 12.\\n")'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
s=s.replace('''T = ed(B, (FENCE + "\\n", ""), ("Run `npm ci` and then `npm run dev`.\\n",
                                "Run `npm ci` and then `npm run dev`.\\n\\n## Components\\n\\n" + FENCE.rstrip("\\n") + "\\n"))''',
'''T = ed(B, (FENCE + "\\n", ""), ("served on port 3000.\\n",
                                "served on port 3000.\\n\\n## Components\\n\\n" + FENCE.rstrip("\\n") + "\\n"))''')
old='''B = ("# CI setup\\n\\nThis repository uses a self-hosted runner.\\n\\n" + FENCE +
     "\\n## Secrets\\n\\nSecrets are injected from the vault at job start.\\n\\n"'''
new='''B = ("# CI setup\\n\\nThis repository uses a self-hosted runner.\\n\\n" + FENCE +
     "\\n## Secrets\\n\\nSecrets are injected from the vault at job start.\\n\\n"
     "| name | used by |\\n|---|---|\\n| `REGISTRY_TOKEN` | image push |\\n"
     "| `CACHE_KEY` | build cache |\\n| `SLACK_HOOK` | notifications |\\n\\n"
     "Rotate them every ninety days.\\n\\n"'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
s=s.replace('''T = ed(B, (FENCE + "\\n", ""), ("injected from the vault at job start.\\n",
                                "injected from the vault at job start.\\n\\n## Pipeline''',
'''T = ed(B, (FENCE + "\\n", ""), ("Rotate them every ninety days.\\n",
                                "Rotate them every ninety days.\\n\\n## Pipeline''')
old='''fx("v30-g3-two-blocks", "F", B, O, T, False, [("G3", ["east", "q", "west"], "B")],'''
new='''fx("v30-g3-two-blocks", "F", B, O, T, False,
   [("G3", ["east", "q", "west"], "B"), ("S-ORDER", ["q", "w_api"], "-"), ("S-ORDER", ["q", "w_db"], "-")],'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
old='''subgraph block, a new L3 failure (no input has it). Not exposed.")'''
new='''subgraph block, a new L3 failure (no input has it). S-ORDER (§5.3, order class): R orders vertices by "
   "first mention. O moves q's first mention after w_api and w_db, T leaves it before them, so the "
   "decided order of each pair is O's; the merged file first mentions q in T's east-block line, before "
   "w_api and w_db. Reported, never eligible. Not exposed.")'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

    ext = "md" if f["stratum"] == "D" else "mmd"
    clean, merged = merge(f["base"], f["o"], f["t"], "diagram." + ext)
    exp_e = any(r[0] == "E" for r in f["records"])
    texts = [f["base"], f["o"], f["t"], merged]
    note = ""
    try:
        if ext == "md":
            fs = [model.fences(x) for x in texts]
            note = "fences=%s " % [len(x) for x in fs]
            dia = [x[0] if len(x) == 1 else None for x in fs]
        else:

        res = None
        if clean and all(dia):
            try:
                res = model.judge(*dia)
            except model.ParseError as e:

        elif not all(dia[:3]):

    except model.ParseError as e:
        note += "PARSE-ERROR %s " % e
        res = None
    status = "clean" if clean else "CONFLICT"
    print("=" * 70)
    print(f["name"], status, note)
    print("  expected:", [(r[0], r[1], r[2]) for r in f["records"]], "exposed", f["exposed"])
    if res:
        print("  model:   ", res["records"], "exposed", res["exposed"])
        print("  newlints:", res["new_lints"])
    if verbose or "-m" in sys.argv:
        print(merged)

# Storefront

The storefront is the customer-facing web application.

## Getting started

You need Node 22 and a running Postgres.

1. Clone the repository.
2. Copy `.env.example` to `.env`.
3. Run `npm ci`.
4. Run `npm run db:migrate`.
5. Run `npm run dev`.

The site is then served on port 3000.

## Components

```mermaid
graph TD
    user([Customer]) --> web[Storefront]
    web --> cart[Cart service]
    cart --> stock[(Inventory)]
    web --> search[Search]
```

## Design notes

Cart and inventory share a database today; see ADR 12.

~~~mermaid
graph TD
    user([Customer]) --> web[Storefront]
    web --> cart[Cart service]
    cart --> stock[(Inventory)]
    web --> search[Search]
~~~

# CI setup

This repository uses a self-hosted runner.

## Secrets

Secrets are injected from the vault at job start.

| name | used by |
|---|---|
| `REGISTRY_TOKEN` | image push |
| `CACHE_KEY` | build cache |
| `SLACK_HOOK` | notifications |

Rotate them every ninety days.

## Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    push[git push] --> hook[Webhook]
    hook --> runner[CI runner]
    runner --> cache[(Build cache)]
    runner --> report[Status check]
    runner --> artifacts[(Artifact store)]
```

       ("    rules --> tsdb\n", "    rules --> influx\n"))

fx("s01", "F", B, O, T, True, [("I1", ["edge", "tsdb"], "A")],
   "O replaces the time-series store tsdb with influx, rewriting all three of its edges (tsdb "
   "removed, §5.1). T adds `edge --> tsdb` so the edge gateway writes directly. I1 (§5.2 dangling, "
   "§5.3 I1): tsdb is decided absent; the edge (edge, tsdb) is decided present (T only) and refers to "
   "it; git merges clean, and tsdb reappears as a node. Objects: tsdb and the keys of the referring "
   "edge. Tier A (§5.4): bare chart, so (L1, tsdb) and (L1, edge) already fail in B and T; nothing is "
   "new. The reappearance is the I1, not a G1. Exposed (§5.5): O removes tsdb, T's added edge refers to "
   "it.")

        "The reset flow, as shipped in release 4.2.",

            flowchart TD
                req([Forgot password]) --> lookup[Find account]
                lookup --> token[Issue reset token]
                token --> mail[Send email]
                mail --> link[User opens link]
                link --> form[New password form]
                form --> hash[Hash and store]

           "    token --> notifier[Notification service]\n    notifier --> link[User opens link]\n"))
T = ed(B, ("    hash --> done([Signed in])\n", "    hash --> done([Signed in])\n    hash --> mail\n"))
fx("s02", "D", B, O, T, True, [("I1", ["hash", "mail"], "B")],
   "O routes the reset email through a notification service, removing mail. T adds `hash --> mail` "
   "(a confirmation email after the change). I1 (§5.2 dangling): mail is decided absent; the edge "
   "(hash, mail) is decided present (T only) and refers to it; clean merge. Tier B (§5.4 row 1): mail "
   "is declared `mail[Send email]` in B and T and has no node statement in the merged file, a new L1 "
   "failure on an object of the record. Exposed: O removes mail, T's edge refers to it.")

# s03 I1, bare, D -> tier A
B = doc("Feature flags",
        "How a flag change reaches clients.",
        d("""
            graph LR
                console --> flagsvc
                flagsvc --> store

import importlib
import json
import os
import shutil
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp/fgen")
import common

CONVENTIONS = """\
## Layout

One directory per case, as Appendix D sets: `base.<ext>`, `o.<ext>`, `t.<ext>`
and `expect.json`. `<ext>` is `mmd` for stratum F and `md` for stratum D. `o` and
`t` are the two legs; the merge is `git merge` of `t` into `o` over `base`
(§6 F2). Merged files are not included: the harness produces them.

`expect.json`:

- `stratum`: `"F"` or `"D"`.
- `exposed`: §5.5, from the three inputs only.
- `records`: every record F expects, each `{"category", "objects"}`.
- `tiers`: one tier per record, in the same order as `records` (`A`, `B`,
  `C`, `D`, `E`, or `—` for categories that are reported only).
- `why`: which rule of §5 decides each record, and the exposure.

A case with no records has `"records": []` and `"tiers": []`.

## Names

- **Categories**: `I1`–`I4`, `G0`–`G4`, `MC`, `C`, `D`, `S-LINKSTYLE`,
  `S-ORDER`, `E`, `DUP-TITLE`.
- **Objects** are keys, sorted: a node id or explicit subgraph id as written,
  `title:` plus the title for a subgraph without an explicit id (§4.1), an
  edge id for a user-defined edge id. The path of the merged file (G0, E) is
  written `<path>`.
- Objects of categories §5.3 does not list: `MC` uses the objects of the
  category whose group it takes (for a relation MC, the edge's two ends).
  `C` and `D` use the key whose unit differs. `S-LINKSTYLE` is one record per
  edge whose `linkStyle` unit differs, with that edge's ends. `S-ORDER` is one
  record per pair of keys out of decided order. `DUP-TITLE` uses the shared
  title key.
- A G2 record does not say "lost" or "extra" in `objects`; `why` says which.

## Readings F applied where §5 leaves a choice

1. **An existence-level record covers its key.** When a case has an I1–I4 or
   G1 record on key `k`, F records no separate G1, G3, G4, C or D for units
   keyed by `k` that differ only because `k` exists, or has a kind, where its
   decided value says otherwise. This extends §5.3 G1's "outside I1–I4" to
   the units keyed by the same key. Identity records do not cover each other:
   a case can hold both I2 and I4 on one key.
2. **Absent is not none.** A unit of a key that does not exist in a state has
   the value *absent*, which differs from `none` (no shape, no holder, no
   style). So a leg that removes a key changes every unit keyed by it.
3. **Order is read pairwise.** §4.2 lists no order unit. F takes, for each
   pair of keys present in all four states, their relative order in R's vertex
   map (first mention). That order is decided per pair by §5.1, and each pair
   whose merged order differs from the decided order is one `S-ORDER` record.
   Keys a leg adds or removes take no part, so adding or deleting a statement
   never yields S-ORDER by itself.
4. **MC eligibility.** "Neither leg's value" is taken literally: a merged value
   equal to `B`'s, but to neither `O`'s nor `T`'s, is eligible.
5. **L5's objects** are the two ends of the duplicated edge (and its edge id,
   if any). A new L5 failure on them demotes a G2 record on that edge to B.
6. **E and G0 stand alone.** An E path gets the single record `E`. A G0 file
   gets the single record `G0`: with two fences there is no one diagram to
   judge.
7. **Single-word subgraph headers.** `subgraph Name` with one word has the
   explicit id `Name` (Appendix A, "`subgraph id`"). Every subgraph that F
   means to be keyed by title has a title of two or more words.

## How the expectations were checked

Every case was merged with stock git 2.47.3 in a fresh repository, under §6
F2's settings (`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, an empty
`HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, no `.gitattributes`). Each clean/conflict outcome
in these files was observed, not assumed. F had no Node.js, so **R was not
run**. Statements about what R parses, and about its model, rest on the
Mermaid 12.1.0 flowchart document and on Appendix A's probes. If R disagrees
with an expectation on an input, that input is wrong and should be reported
back to F; it is not evidence about H.

## Licence

All files here are synthetic, written by F for this experiment, and dedicated
to the public domain under CC0-1.0. No text was taken from any repository.
"""


def write_set(mods, outdir, title, intro, index):
    common.FIX.clear()
    for m in mods:
        importlib.import_module(m)
    for f in common.FIX:
        ext = "md" if f["stratum"] == "D" else "mmd"
        cdir = os.path.join(outdir, f["name"])
        os.makedirs(cdir, exist_ok=False)
        for part in ("base", "o", "t"):
            with open(os.path.join(cdir, f"{part}.{ext}"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                fh.write(f[part])
        recs = [{"category": c, "objects": sorted(o)} for c, o, _ in f["records"]]
        tiers = ["—" if t == "-" else t for _, _, t in f["records"]]
        exp = {"stratum": f["stratum"], "exposed": f["exposed"], "records": recs, "tiers": tiers, "why": f["why"]}
        with open(os.path.join(cdir, "expect.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as fh:
            json.dump(exp, fh, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
            fh.write("\n")
    lines = [f"# {title}\n", intro, CONVENTIONS]
    if index:
        lines.append("## Index\n\n| case | stratum | exposed | records (tier) |\n|---|---|---|---|\n")
        for f in common.FIX:
            r = ", ".join(f"{c} {'/'.join(sorted(o))} ({'—' if t == '-' else t})" for c, o, t in f["records"]) or "none (clean)"
            lines.append(f"| `{f['name']}` | {f['stratum']} | {'yes' if f['exposed'] else 'no'} | {r} |\n")
    with open(os.path.join(outdir, "README.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(l.rstrip("\n") + "\n" for l in lines))
    return list(common.FIX)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    which = sys.argv[1]
    if which == "v":
        fx = write_set(["v_identity", "v_structure", "v_other"], "/work/v-fixtures", "V-fixtures",
                       "Fixtures for V1, V3 and V5 (§10.4, §11.2), written by F, the fixture author.\n",
                       index=True)
    else:
        fx = write_set(["s_defs"], "/work/sealed", "Sealed fixtures",
                       "Sealed fixtures (§10.4), written by F. Held by the owner until commit 6.\n",
                       index=False)
    print(len(fx), "cases written")

import importlib
import json
import os
import shutil
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp/fgen")
import common

CONVENTIONS = """\
## Layout

One directory per case, as Appendix D sets: `base.<ext>`, `o.<ext>`, `t.<ext>`
and `expect.json`. `<ext>` is `mmd` for stratum F and `md` for stratum D. `o` and
`t` are the two legs; the merge is `git merge` of `t` into `o` over `base`
(§6 F2). Merged files are not included: the harness produces them.

`expect.json`:

- `stratum`: `"F"` or `"D"`.
- `exposed`: §5.5, from the three inputs only.
- `records`: every record F expects, each `{"category", "objects"}`.
- `tiers`: one tier per record, in the same order as `records` (`A`, `B`,
  `C`, `D`, `E`, or `—` for categories that are reported only).
- `why`: which rule of §5 decides each record, and the exposure.

A case with no records has `"records": []` and `"tiers": []`.

## Names

- **Categories**: `I1`–`I4`, `G0`–`G4`, `MC`, `C`, `D`, `S-LINKSTYLE`,
  `S-ORDER`, `E`, `DUP-TITLE`.
- **Objects** are keys, sorted: a node id or explicit subgraph id as written,
  `title:` plus the title for a subgraph without an explicit id (§4.1), an
  edge id for a user-defined edge id. The path of the merged file (G0, E) is
  written `<path>`.
- Objects of categories §5.3 does not list: `MC` uses the objects of the
  category whose group it takes (for a relation MC, the edge's two ends).
  `C` and `D` use the key whose unit differs. `S-LINKSTYLE` is one record per
  edge whose `linkStyle` unit differs, with that edge's ends. `S-ORDER` is one
  record per pair of keys out of decided order. `DUP-TITLE` uses the shared
  title key.
- A G2 record does not say "lost" or "extra" in `objects`; `why` says which.

## Readings F applied where §5 leaves a choice

1. **An existence-level record covers its key.** When a case has an I1–I4 or
   G1 record on key `k`, F records no separate G1, G3, G4, C or D for units
   keyed by `k` that differ only because `k` exists, or has a kind, where its
   decided value says otherwise. This extends §5.3 G1's "outside I1–I4" to
   the units keyed by the same key. Identity records do not cover each other:
   a case can hold both I2 and I4 on one key.

   the value *absent*, which differs from `none` (no shape, no holder, no
   style). So a leg that removes a key changes every unit keyed by it.
3. **Order is read pairwise.** §4.2 lists no order unit. F takes, for each
   pair of keys present in all four states, their relative order in R's vertex
   map (first mention). That order is decided per pair by §5.1, and each pair
   whose merged order differs from the decided order is one `S-ORDER` record.

   never yields S-ORDER by itself.

import model
for root in ('/work/v-fixtures','/work/sealed'):
    cov=collections.defaultdict(set); bad=[]; n=0; exposedE=0; clean=0; strata=collections.Counter()
    for c in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        p=os.path.join(root,c)
        if not os.path.isdir(p): continue
        n+=1
        e=json.load(open(os.path.join(p,'expect.json'),encoding='utf-8'))
        ext='md' if e['stratum']=='D' else 'mmd'
        txt=[open(os.path.join(p,f'{x}.{ext}'),newline='',encoding='utf-8').read() for x in ('base','o','t')]
        ok,merged=merge(*txt,'diagram.'+ext)
        cats=[r['category'] for r in e['records']]
        assert len(e['tiers'])==len(cats)
        isE='E' in cats
        # E either from git conflict or R parse failure
        parsefail=False
        if ok:
            try:
                dia=[model.fences(x) for x in txt+[merged]] if ext=='md' else [[x] for x in txt+[merged]]
                if len(dia[3])==1: model.parse(dia[3][0])
            except model.ParseError: parsefail=True
        if isE != ((not ok) or parsefail): bad.append(c)
        if ext=='md':
            for x in txt: assert len(model.fences(x))==1, c
        strata[e['stratum']]+=1

EOF

src, out_tar, out_nonce = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
files = []
for dp, dn, fn in os.walk(src):
    for f in fn:
        full = os.path.join(dp, f)
        files.append((os.path.join("sealed", os.path.relpath(full, src)).replace(os.sep, "/"), full))

**Stop rule:** this directory held only the pre-registration, the Mermaid doc and two empty folders. I found no harness code, repository history or `.git`, and nothing was fetched.

**What I wrote**
- **`v-fixtures/`:** 65 cases (38 in stratum F, 27 in D), each in the Appendix D layout. Every category in §10.4 has at least three fixtures, plus 3 exposed cases that git refuses and 10 clean cases. They also cover the V3 plants: both holes in both styles and both strata, positional subgraph ids, the five "membership is not a reference" cases, duplicate titles, an edge to a subgraph, the relative-I4 case, the per-path E case, and the fence variants. Both strata are covered except G0, which only stratum D can produce. `v-fixtures/README.md` indexes every case.
- **`sealed/`:** 13 cases across both strata: 3 I1 (two in bare style, tier A), 2 I2, 1 I3, 3 structure (G1, G2, G3), 2 B ghosts that L1 sees, and 2 clean.
- **`why`:** each fixture's `why` names the §5 rule behind each record, its tier and its exposure.

**Delivery to the owner:** the tar and nonce are in `/home/role/owner-only/` (`sealed.tar`, `nonce.bin`). The directory is readable only by its owner, outside `/work`, and the nonce was never printed. Repacking gives byte-identical output, and the hash recomputes from the stored files.

**Before you go on**

- **Mermaid was never run.** Node.js isn't installed here, so whether R parses each input rests on the Mermaid doc and Appendix A. Every merge, though, was a real `git merge` (git 2.47.3) under §6 F2's hermetic settings, so each clean or conflict outcome was observed, not assumed. V0/V1 would show any input R rejects.
- **I made seven choices where §5 is open, listed in the README.** The four that matter most:
  - An I1–I4 or G1 record on a key covers that key's own label, shape, membership and style differences.
  - "Absent" is a different value from "none".
  - Order is compared pairwise, by first mention, among keys present in all four states.
  - An MC whose merged value equals the base's still counts as eligible.

  H or X may read these differently. Only the V-fixture README states them, so V5 will show any disagreement before the sealed run. The sealed expectations follow the same choices.
- **The `expect.json` format adds a few conventions of mine.** `tiers` is a list parallel to `records`. `<path>` is the object for G0 and E records. Tier `—` marks the categories that are only reported.
